scope: Grades 1–6, formal grade-end source duties; primary authoring through age 12. Grade concepts remain required; parenthetical examples are illustrative.
meaning: Original authored task portfolios, not reproduced curriculum passages, tested interventions or learner attainment. A component association alone never certifies a whole expectation. Actual required making/performance, creator/audience response and source-specific context/resource conditions remain in the portfolio.

protocols.title: Own expressive movement and revision
protocols.task: Use an original brief story or poem and a daily/natural action as two distinct stimuli. The learner chooses, connects, practises and performs an own phrase, then changes a spatial or movement-quality choice for another meaning. Keep a trial and revised version. Apply the selected grade panel: changed familiar action/body shapes and links; pathways and deliberate opening/ending; patterned sections; narrative structure; call-and-response with a partner; or guided improvisation and safe props.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The actual phrase has owned choices, meaningful order and a demonstrated purposeful change. The task contains the particular grade-panel operation, not merely general movement.
protocols.nearMiss: Copying isolated actions, exercise skill or naming a dance element without composing/performing does not establish the source operation.
protocols.transfer: Use a new original stimulus and adapt the phrase; the intended meaning may be indicated through demonstration or ordinary language.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual source-specific elements and structures retained; safe accessible movement, no fixed athletic norm or compulsory cultural imitation.

protocols.title: Evidence-based interpretation of movement
protocols.task: View two short contrasting versions of a teacher/peer original phrase and a lawfully available professional excerpt. Describe what actually changes in body, space, time, energy or relationship and connect observed details to a possible meaning. For literature-linked records compare the source idea with the actual movement interpretation. Keep first impression and reasoned response distinct.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner points to a visible choice and supports an interpretation; junior panels use appropriate dance vocabulary and compare effects rather than merely say a favourite.
protocols.nearMiss: An emotion label with no visible evidence, universal shape-to-emotion rule or discussion without viewing the actual movement is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Interpret a new phrase and allow a defensible different response supported by movement evidence.
protocols.sourceConditions: Source-specific body/space/time/energy/relationship vocabulary and actual own/others work; no compulsory liking.

protocols.title: Specific improvement in actual arts work
protocols.task: After an actual piece and audience experience, identify a concrete strength, one interest and a useful next step with evidence from that work. Try the step or explain a reasoned alternative. Where feedback is linked, give a partner one specific positive and a respectful suggestion, receive feedback and constructively use or assess it.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner names the actual decision/process and shows a meaningful next move; creator and audience duties both have a case.
protocols.nearMiss: A generic claim of being good/bad, compulsory cheerfulness or a wish with no process example does not establish reflection.
protocols.transfer: Apply the reflection process to another work or audience role.
protocols.sourceConditions: Retain documentation where the source requires it and whole two-way feedback checks where linked. Disappointment is not failure. The whole two-way feedback task is an available supplementary learning route; a self-reflection source record is linked to reflection, not automatically to every feedback operation.

protocols.title: Attributed dances in their settings
protocols.task: Compare the Mi’kmaq round-dance account shared by Richard and Julie Pellissier-Lush in the NAC Amalkay guide, Red Sky’s contemporary Trace and the Versailles court-dance account. Attribute each distinct people/creator, time, place and stated purpose. Use actual permitted images/excerpts; a text description alone is not a viewed-performance claim. For Grade 6 Indigenous past/present duties retain the Mi’kmaq transmission/gathering case alongside the contemporary Anishinaabe-inspired work; do not conflate their traditions. Include a supplied local school/community dance occasion when a personal experience is not volunteered.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner describes actual distinguishing forms/purposes and compares social/community/historical roles using attributed evidence. Junior panels explain the requested context relation rather than only name a dance.
protocols.nearMiss: Treating all Indigenous peoples as one, presenting a court practice as universal, claiming a fictional ritual or forcing personal/religious participation is invalid.
protocols.transfer: Use another attributed public example or examine how a contemporary audience/media encounter differs from the court/gathering context.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual resource rights/access and attribution must be retained; no ceremonial imitation required. Historical and contemporary contexts are not collapsed.

protocols.title: Role-based improvisation and scene development
protocols.task: Use an original classroom story about neighbours planning a safe delivery after a bridge closes. Participants adopt different roles, perspectives and relationships, improvise a changed situation, plan together in/out of role and rehearse a short scene. Make a deliberate setting, tension or focus choice. Add a familiar poem/script performance separately to account for the complete existing performance claim. The portfolio includes an original contemporary classroom fiction, an attributed public-domain Aesop fable, and a nonfiction exploration of the checked Versailles court account. Read/view the source, identify what it establishes and keep improvised dialogue distinct from historical quotation. The Mi’kmaq guide’s publicly shared family/gathering context may support an ordinary respectful social-role scene; no learner is required to enact a sacred figure or ceremony.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The scene contains actual role choices, responses to partners and an owned dramatic decision, not only a read-aloud. Script, poem and changed-situation improvisation are separately observed in the authored protocol.
protocols.nearMiss: Reciting a line flatly, copying an adult solution or supplying only a character description cannot establish actual drama production.
protocols.transfer: Change a character goal or setting and adapt the scene while retaining the agreed role context.
protocols.sourceConditions: Whole performance card retained; no personal trauma disclosure or independent-reading demand added to the source. Safe unfamiliar roles are supplied. Actual diverse community/time/place sources and fiction/nonfiction panels are used; a single invented bridge story alone is insufficient. Select a secular alternative without erasing the source variety.

protocols.title: Intentional technical support for meaning
protocols.task: Present the scene twice using simple safe props, images, sound or light choices to change a specified dramatic effect for an audience. Learners select and operate accessible aids, explain/show the intended change and compare the audience’s evidenced interpretations.
protocols.positiveEvidence: A purposeful aid actually contributes to the performed meaning; junior work addresses the particular audience/effect.
protocols.nearMiss: A technology list, decorative prop or merely describing lighting is not its use in a performance.
protocols.transfer: Use a different safe aid for a changed audience or scene effect and compare.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual audio/visual/technology duty retained according to the record; examples do not prescribe hazardous lighting or particular equipment.

protocols.title: Interpreting a dramatic choice
protocols.task: View an original short scene and a changed version, then respond with a drawing, discussion or supported written account. Refer to character, setting, relationship, tension and focus as applicable; support interpretation with details from the performance. For the complete existing drama-analysis card, compare two productions of a short accessible script and how each realises/departs from it, retaining textual-evidence hard-chain tasks separately.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The response supports an interpretation by observed dramatic choices and makes the required personal/theme connection.
protocols.nearMiss: A preference without reasons, plot retelling alone or one lighting label does not show how performance makes meaning.
protocols.transfer: Use a new short scene or a contrasting production and justify a different plausible interpretation.
protocols.sourceConditions: Do not lower the full advanced inherited analysis chain merely because a primary diagnostic is short; retain it as conditional where complete source-fit cannot be qualified.

protocols.title: Theatre forms, work and cultural purposes
protocols.task: Use the attributed public Mi’kmaq Legends account in the NAC guide, an actual accessible local/community production and the UNESCO Wayang documentary/archive account (Indonesia,2008). Compare form, role, storytelling and context; for Grade 5 explicitly describe producer, director, actor, stage manager, designer and technical duties using a real production’s credits. For Grade 6 include concrete community functions and the actual contemporary Indigenous theatre case. For professional duties, use the actual RSC Stage Management and Theatres Trust job accounts, then trace a changed audience/venue cue to a changed coordination duty. Keep the existing roles claim’s distinct environmental-care transfer check separate from theatre facts.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner connects actual formal features and people’s work to context/purpose, with the required variety.
protocols.nearMiss: A generic culture list, role clothing or a fictional attribution does not establish theatre-context knowledge.
protocols.transfer: Compare another actual production or change the production role to explain its contribution.
protocols.sourceConditions: The actual UNESCO archive body confirms the Indonesian puppetry forms and court/rural contexts; viewing or object-image access remains required for the task, not merely a national label.

protocols.title: Actual repertoire and musicianship
protocols.task: Use an attributed accessible selection with the NAC Music Alive score/audio and a contrasting recorded work. Learners actually sing and play an accessible accompaniment, coordinate a part with others and apply the required pitch, rhythm, dynamics, timbre, texture and form. The chosen grade/source panel retains unison/parts/notation requirements and safe appropriate breathing, posture or instrument handling. The actual vocal/playing selection spans Sherryl Sewepagaham’s Music Alive (contemporary Cree/English), Olivia Tailfeathers’s Blackfoot song shared in the credited NAC Celebrating guide, and the Beethoven finale theme arranged in the NAC unit. Prepare the actual linked scores and lawful audio, pronunciation/context support and comfortable accessible parts; no forced personal identity or positive feeling. Use the available two-part canon/Orff ensemble and supplementary score tasks for the required grade duties, not a lone tapped beat as all repertoire.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual audible performance contains the declared part, accurate musical relationships and responsive coordination; naming terms alone is insufficient.
protocols.nearMiss: A tapped beat offered as complete pitched singing, solo success offered as ensemble coordination or an invented-symbol task offered as staff reading is incomplete.
protocols.transfer: Use a changed phrase, part or instrument within safe access; retain original work attribution and cultural context.
protocols.sourceConditions: A primary source repertoire matrix must check every applicable fundamental-concept category. No fixed instrument, vocal range norm or competition criterion.
protocols.additionalConcreteTaskSpecification: reports/assets/ontario-arts-programme/repertoire.json contains the actual canon, supplied I/V then I/IV/V progression, interval contrasts and original sectional/variation tasks. Bind the appropriate actual source-grade portfolio; no miniature alone proves the whole repertoire.

protocols.title: Own sounded work for an intended audience
protocols.task: Create and present an original short accompaniment or musical scene for the original bridge story. Try alternative sound/silence choices, listen and revise timing, timbre, dynamic or phrase structure for a stated purpose and audience. Bind the actual grade form/element duties. Preserve standard notation separately where required.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Own audible choices and a purposeful audible revision are present. Repetition is musically legitimate; formal mathematical complexity is not the criterion.
protocols.nearMiss: Copying a sounded adult answer, only explaining an AB rule or displaying notes with no audible piece is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Adapt the work to a different scene, audience or available safe source and compare the intended effect.
protocols.sourceConditions: Source-specific phrase/form/harmony and actual composition requirements are not inferred from a single free-improvisation example.

protocols.title: Reversible musical representation
protocols.task: Use the concrete original A–E staff panels and exact event keys. Grade 1/2 source tasks use a stable key for unheard equal-pulse timbre/silence patterns and own encoding with partner recovery. Grade 3 includes actual standard duration/rest signs AND a devised representation. Grade 4–6 requires actual conventional staff reading/recording and its applicable key, metre, marking and repertoire duties.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The score is actually recovered and a new intended sequence is recorded for someone else; changed-sign diagnosis and a new-score transfer occur.
protocols.nearMiss: Invented-key success never establishes complete standard staff literacy; note naming alone is not performance or composition.
protocols.transfer: Use another short unheard score and translate between a devised representation and staff score without erasing the required musical information.
protocols.sourceConditions: The reviewed fixed staff claim is now authored as mt_Gy9nCgUjlD at its exact G4–6 source bands. Early devised representation remains a component task and never certifies the whole fixed staff operation. The additional original F/G/H/J scores have been rendered and checked against their event keys; they remain parts of the wider repertoire programme.

protocols.title: Music choices and supported personal response
protocols.task: Listen to actual contrasting works/excerpts with different observable duration, pitch, timbre, texture, form or expressive controls. Give an own response through words, movement or image, then identify heard features that support an interpretation. Junior responses use relevant terminology and reasoned comparison; no single emotion is deemed universal.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner makes an actual listening-based observation and supports a response with musical evidence.
protocols.nearMiss: A genre label, compulsory pleasant feeling or sound-physics explanation does not establish musical interpretation.
protocols.transfer: Listen to a new excerpt and support a different plausible response with its actual features.
protocols.sourceConditions: Physics pitch/volume is not a mandatory proxy. Repertoire and audition access remain explicit.

protocols.title: Attributed musical communities and influence
protocols.task: Compare NAC’s attributed contemporary Music Alive/Indigenous-creator material with an actual classical-era recording and its checked context. Add the UMS Playing Along with Gamelan artist-facilitated resource for the appropriate junior panel for broader variety. Examine where each is used, who makes it and its function. Junior panels use an actual media/advertising example and compare particular styles or historical/community roles as requested. The concrete media task is an original classroom advertisement for a community event: present the same words/images with two different short original musical accompaniments and compare the impressions supported by their heard features. It is an authored comparison task, not an empirical general claim about advertising efficacy.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner describes heard examples and their particular context/function; artistic differences are not explained by a stereotype.
protocols.nearMiss: A universal taste hierarchy, unattributed recording or a general claim that every community uses music identically is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Use another actual attributed work or a changed media setting and compare evidence about use or influence.
protocols.sourceConditions: NAC provides actual attributed contemporary and classical recordings/score references. UMS gamelan is an actual artist-facilitated resource recommended forGrades3–10; primary6–7 tasks do not import its older worksheet or ritual/deity activities. Actual musical observation and context are checked; no universal taste or Indigenous-belief rule.

protocols.title: Own 2D and 3D compositions
protocols.task: Produce an own flat composition and a small three-dimensional assemblage or modelled form based on an original experience/story/theme. Choose visual elements, try an alternative arrangement and revise for intended meaning. For Grade 6 include an actual accessible multimedia work. Use the grade-specific principles/elements as actual decisions, not only vocabulary.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner makes and changes own visual arrangements in the required forms; the effect is shown in the work rather than copied from an adult model.
protocols.nearMiss: Controlled marks alone, an adult-cut identical product or a written description replacing the actual three-dimensional/multimedia work is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Adapt the composition to a new intention, available material or viewing space and indicate the changed choices.
protocols.sourceConditions: No aesthetic-quality norm or universal colour-to-feeling code; source-specific 2D/3D/multimedia duties remain actual.

protocols.title: Actual varied tools and design solutions
protocols.task: Prepare three accessible contrasting stations: drawing/painting with tested pigment mixtures, value and mark changes;a print/collage arrangement;and a safe modelled/assembled form. Respond to an original visual challenge through actual handling and comparisons. Retain the selected grade’s colour, space, texture, value and design-principle duties; illustrative named techniques are not all compulsory.
protocols.positiveEvidence: Actual tool/material choices produce a relevant visual effect and the learner adjusts a solution.
protocols.nearMiss: A colour-name quiz, one unexamined medium or only a functional engineering product does not show the visual challenge duty.
protocols.transfer: Change a material or visual constraint and adjust the handling/composition accordingly.
protocols.sourceConditions: Safe prepared access; no industrial tools. Grade 1 primary pigment and later tint/shade/complementary/tertiary duties need actual mixtures, not light-physics substitution.

protocols.title: Interpretation grounded in actual visual choices
protocols.task: View The Enchanted Owl in the attributed museum record and Monet’s Bridge over a Pond of Water Lilies in the Met record, alongside actual own/peer work. Describe visual evidence, interpret a possible meaning and relate a personal response; compare how particular arrangements support effects. Use the actual applicable design vocabulary.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner refers to line, form, space, colour, texture or value and relevant design principles to support an interpretation.
protocols.nearMiss: Repeating a supplied mood, only naming a colour or claiming an artist intended something not established by evidence is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Respond to another attributed work and compare a defensible alternative interpretation.
protocols.sourceConditions: No universal colour/emotion rule or inference of all Inuit perspectives from one artist. Images are linked with their rights, not republished without permission.

protocols.title: Signs, symbols, style and community function
protocols.task: Use actual attributed symbols in artworks and everyday communications with supplied culturally accurate meanings. Compare an ordinary contextual sign with an artwork’s symbolic or stylistic use and explain how audience/context affects interpretation. Combine the museum examples with a real local gallery/public-art/community-programme case and an actual credited visual/media arts occupation. Concrete contextual symbols are Andrew Qappik’s Nunavut flag (official Assembly explanation of inuksuk/star) and the Canadian maple leaf (Governor General heraldic record). Compare these stated meanings with an original pupil-made symbol whose intended meaning is supplied by its maker; do not guess a universal colour or animal meaning. For Grade 6 D3.2, compare the actual school/class exhibition, where student creators share ideas with their immediate audience, with the Canadian national flag’s public identity/symbol function in the Governor General’s official heraldic record (project 462). Use the actual flag image through that official resource; do not substitute a performing-arts institution for a visual/media-arts case. Include Kenojuak Ashevak’s credited artist role in the MMFA Enchanted Owl record as the concrete visual-arts occupation case, distinguishing an artist’s work from the exhibition audience. National identity is an attributed function of this particular flag design, not a universal meaning for maple leaves or all Canadian art.
protocols.positiveEvidence: The learner interprets the concrete symbol/style in its context and explains a requested historical/community/function relation with evidence.
protocols.nearMiss: Treating one colour meaning as global, claiming a decorative shape always means the same thing or inventing local history is invalid.
protocols.transfer: Compare another checked symbol/style or a different audience/context and explain the limits of transfer.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual supplied school/class artworks and credited institutional examples support the task; application binds the learner’s own local encounter without inventing a visit. Public flag meanings are attributed to their official sources, not generalised to every Inuit artwork. No private belief disclosure or unlicensed copied image.

gradePanels.task: Transform reaching for a shelf and moving a box into an own short phrase. Choose whole-body and isolated-part movement, a distinct supported base and two contrasting shapes. Travel through a marked safe personal/general space, change level and direction, then contrast moving/freezing and fast/slow rhythm. Make a sustained version and a light percussive version. Mirror a partner without requiring contact. Ask which actual choice changed the intended message.
gradePanels.conditions: Use actual safe accessible materials/performance and the exact source record duty. Examples are selected concrete implementations, not a new checklist of every parenthetical source example. Prior concepts continue; collect a portfolio rather than claim one miniature proves the whole area.
gradePanels.evidence: Retain the actual work/performance, a meaningful maker revision, an independently recoverable or explained detail, and a changed transfer case. No aesthetic quality, positive feeling, body/vision norm or spontaneous unpractised expert performance threshold.

conditions.actualPerformance: Use actual own artwork, audible performance, movement or role-play. Naming vocabulary or viewing an adult performance does not substitute for an own production duty.
conditions.resourceBinding: Prepare the linked attributed lawful excerpts, original score assets and safe accessible materials. Local/own-life duties use actual class/home/community encounters and original work, not an invented visit or assumed family belief; no private disclosure is required.
conditions.sourceStatus: This is the 2009 Ontario source, not the NCERT framework or a source clone. No compulsory affect, cultural imitation or universal artistic taste/colour-response rule.
conditions.wholeClaimBoundary: Where linked, preserve each existing whole claim’s independent assessment/transfer. Supplementary whole-card checks are not newly declared Ontario duties. Parallel projection, physics of pitch/light, feeling labels and a mathematical repeat rule are not automatic substitutes for artistic operations.
conditions.thirdPartyRights: Third-party songs, lyrics, images and scores remain linked resources with their attribution/permission limits; only original task resources are stored here.
conditions.onePointConstruction: Grade6 D1.3 uses the actual one-point construction/repair/changed-view task and original A–D diagrams. The older parallel-projection claim remains unchanged, retains its old ages and is not a substitute or new prerequisite.

sharedClaimAssessmentBoundaries.check: Keep an actual supplied script performance, poem performance and a separate changed-situation improvisation. Voice, action, silence/stillness and revision remain; one tableau alone does not demonstrate the whole existing claim.

In the actual collaborative scene, contribute an idea, attend and respond to a partner, build on it and complete an agreed fair part. Separate turn-taking and listening evidence remains; no group member’s success is inferred from the group product. Disappointment is compatible with fair action.

Describe attributed distinct practices and formulate an actual respectful question. Discuss what was learned and why avoiding assumptions helps a community. Separate whole-card social comparison/inclusion scenarios remain available; an artwork label never proves the full inherited social or affective claims. No compulsory liking, smile, personal disclosure or invented internal feeling is inferred.

Compare an actual initial plan and the process after a meaningful chosen revision or changed task constraint. Identify a concrete support and next process change, and state confusion truthfully if any; do not manufacture frustration or infer a gap from a pleasant or difficult mood.

State a response and support it with an observed work detail, present the interpretation and explain thinking rather than only a one-word answer. Source-permitted movement/visual responses remain, but alone do not certify the complete existing spoken discussion/presentation claim.

Describe actual theatre workers’ duties using the professional accounts, then explain a changed venue/audience circumstance. Retain the full existing across-setting/environmental-care transfer assessment separately; theatre-role names alone do not certify it.

For the selected early repeating sound/icon task identify the core, continue/create/compare it and translate it to objects/letters. Use a new repeat for transfer. A finite ABA/rondo composition is not automatically the mathematical repeating unit, and staff literacy is not inferred.

local.function: Share actual student visual ideas with an immediate school/community audience; retain the real work and encounter rather than invent a gallery visit.
